content: Lingui ships an ESLint plugin for catching macro-usage errors, but 'no hardcoded string' enforcement itself typically requires a separate literal-string-detection plugin (e.g. eslint-plugin-i18next's no-literal-string rule pattern, or a purpose-built i18n linter) layered on top, since Lingui's own plugin does not by default flag plain JSX text/string literals that were never wrapped in t()/Trans.
